text:
Together, they provided farmland and a residence for Cheng. This angered the elder brothers, who viewed it as a hollow display of generosity. They went to Cheng's home to harass and insult him. Having spent a long time among bandits, Cheng was accustomed to forceful and fierce behavior. Hearing their insults, he grew furious and said, "Now that I have returned, no one was willing to provide me with a roof over my head. Fortunately, my third brother cared for our sibling bond, yet you now punish him for it? Do you intend to drive me away?" 

He threw a stone at Xiao <note>The eldest brother</note>. Ren and Yi <note>The second and third brothers</note> both came out with staffs. Cheng seized Zhong and Xin <note>The sons of the elder brothers</note> and beat them both countless times. Before they could bring a lawsuit against him, Cheng sued them first. The magistrate sent someone to consult Youyu <note>The youngest brother</note>. Youyu had no choice but to go. He stated that he was deeply ashamed of himself and remained silent, only weeping. When pressed for an answer, he only begged the official to deliver a just verdict. The magistrate then ruled that Xiao and the others must each give up a portion of their farmland and property to Cheng, so that the estate was divided into seven equal parts. 

From this point on, Ren and Yi showed Cheng even greater love and respect than before. During a conversation, they suddenly spoke of their mother's burial, and all three wept. Cheng said with determination, "To be so unkind as to leave her thus is to be no better than a beast." He then wished to open the grave and rebury her. Ren and Yi ran to tell Youyu. Youyu hurried home to advise against it, but Cheng would not listen and set a date for the task.

<summary>Cheng violently defends himself against his elder brothers' harassment and wins a legal settlement for his share of the family estate. He later insists on reburying his mother despite Youyu's objections.</summary>
<keywords>Liaozhai Zhiyi, Pu Songling, family dispute, inheritance, filial piety, legal judgment, reburial</keywords>
